name: WiZ Color A19 (US)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi with Bluetooth Low Energy (used for setup).

matter.note: Unconfirmed for code 046677603441. Its own page says only 'Matter: via 3rd party hubs'; the 3-pack page says 'Matter certified'. We found no CSA or WiZ list entry for this exact product code.

apple_home.note: WiZ lists no HomeKit support (Siri Shortcuts is not Apple Home). Apple Home would need Matter, which is unconfirmed for this product code.

google_home.note: Works through WiZ's Google Home integration.

alexa.note: Works through the WiZ Alexa skill.

smartthings.note: WiZ lists Samsung SmartThings among compatible platforms.

home_assistant.note: Official WiZ integration (local push). Requires 'Allow local communication' in the WiZ app, which is on by default.

hubRequired.note: For bulbs, this means needing a bridge or hub for basic app control. The bulb joins Wi-Fi directly and is controlled from the WiZ app.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's WiZ integration controls bulbs over the LAN (local push).

colorType.note: Full colour plus tunable white from 2200 to 6500 K.

lumens.note: 800 lm nominal at 8.8 W (60 W equivalent).

summary: For Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings, the WiZ Color A19 needs nothing but your Wi-Fi: it connects over 2.4 GHz, uses Bluetooth for setup, and each platform works through WiZ's own integration. Home Assistant's official WiZ integration controls it locally. This US bulb (product code 046677603441) has an E26 base and gives 800 lumens at 8.8 W, a 60 W equivalent, with full colour and white from 2200 to 6500 K. Apple Home is unconfirmed, since WiZ lists no HomeKit support and Matter isn't confirmed for this code.
caveats: No confirmed Apple Home route: WiZ lists no HomeKit support, and Siri Shortcuts isn't the same as Apple Home.
WiZ's own pages disagree on Matter: this bulb's page says 'via 3rd party hubs', while the 3-pack page says 'Matter certified'.
Home Assistant needs 'Allow local communication' enabled in the WiZ app; it's on by default.
